name: firebase

platform.name: Firebase
platform.why: firebase.json declares hosting, functions, Firestore, Realtime Database and Storage; .github/workflows/firebase-deploy.yml runs firebase deploy

stays.note: hosting source is the repository root: a Next.js app deployed with the webframeworks experiment (enabled in .github/workflows/firebase-deploy.yml); pages/admin/[experiment_id].js has getServerSideProps, so Firebase builds an SSR function for it
onRequest, onSchedule, onTaskDispatched, Firestore and Realtime Database triggers from firebase-functions/v2; one 1st gen auth trigger (functions/src/on-user-deleted.ts, firebase-functions/v1/auth)

notBreaks.why: a lease heartbeat setInterval that lives only for the duration of one request and is cleared in a finally block; Cloud Scheduler (onSchedule) does the scheduled work
a one-off developer script that writes a token file locally
a maintenance script that vendors a package into functions/metadata/ before a build
test code; session( is a test helper, not express-session

notes: Everything server-side is already serverless on Google: Firebase Hosting (a Next.js app via the webframeworks experiment, with one getServerSideProps page) and Cloud Functions, all firebase-functions/v2 except the 1st gen auth onDelete trigger in functions/src/on-user-deleted.ts. Scheduled work runs on Cloud Scheduler (scheduled-sweep.ts, scheduled-token-refresh.ts) and queued work on Cloud Tasks (onTaskDispatched), so there is no worker or clock to move. migrations/*.cjs are one-off Firestore data migrations run by hand from .github/workflows/run-migration.yml, not a release step. packages/client is a browser client library published to npm; lib/ and components/ are the Next.js front end. functions/src/mock-server.ts is an Express mock used by the emulator tests.

known.FALSE break: in-process-timer functions/: a timer that only keeps a lease, a health check or an in-memory cache fresh; the rule sees a setInterval or send_after and cannot read what the callback does, so it keeps the finding and the person decides (a lease heartbeat for one request, cleared in a finally block)
